rules: INSPIRE Index Polygons is an open-source HM Land Registry dataset developed to comply with the INSPIRE Directive.
INSPIRE Index Polygons contains locations of freehold registered property in England and Wales.
INSPIRE Index Polygons is a subset of HMLR's Index Polygons database for all freehold land and property.
HMLR divides INSPIRE Index Polygons into separate data files for each local authority area in England and Wales.
A polygon on a boundary between local authorities can appear in both local-authority INSPIRE files.
INSPIRE polygons show the position and indicative extent of a registered property rather than an exact legal boundary.
Each INSPIRE Index Polygon has a unique Land Registry-INSPIRE ID.
The Land Registry-INSPIRE ID relates an INSPIRE polygon to a registered title.
HMLR says an INSPIRE ID can be used with Find a Property to obtain title registration and plan information.
Use of INSPIRE Index Polygons under the Open Government Licence is free.
HMLR states that failure to comply with OGL conditions ends the reuse rights granted under the licence.
OGL reuse of HMLR INSPIRE data requires an HMLR Crown copyright/database-right attribution statement.
Reuse of INSPIRE polygon geometry also requires an Ordnance Survey Crown copyright/database-right attribution statement.
HMLR asks reusers to link to the INSPIRE conditions where possible.
The INSPIRE dataset is updated on the first Sunday of each month.
A monthly INSPIRE publication shows data from the previous month.
The current INSPIRE files remain accessible until the following monthly publication replaces them.
HMLR publishes INSPIRE Index Polygon files as GML.
HMLR states that a GIS is needed to view the downloaded INSPIRE polygons.
A GIS can store or edit the downloaded HMLR data and compare or integrate it with other datasets.
The current indexed INSPIRE download was published on 5 July 2026.
The current INSPIRE download index offers polygons by local authority.
Downloading current INSPIRE polygon files is subject to the OGL conditions of use.
HMLR captures its polygon data against the British National Grid.
Each point composing an HMLR polygon is represented by X and Y values referenced to British National Grid.
Using HMLR polygons in web mapping tools can require reprojection from British National Grid.
HMLR guidance identifies British National Grid as EPSG:27700 for reprojection workflows.
HMLR gives WGS 84 Pseudo Mercator EPSG:3857 as an example target CRS used by Google and Bing maps.
HMLR warns that projection conversion calculations can introduce positional error.
HMLR warns that British National Grid to WGS84 conversion can shift some data features by up to 15 metres.
HMLR describes GML as an open data format widely used across Europe.
HMLR states that GML complies with the EU INSPIRE Directive.
HMLR says it supports open standards and uses GML to provide a standard structure across GIS/CAD systems.
HMLR guidance says GML can be converted into ESRI Shapefile.
HMLR guidance says GML can be converted into MapInfo MIF or TAB.
HMLR guidance says GML can be converted into AutoCAD DXF.
HMLR guidance says GML can be converted into GeoJSON.
HMLR guidance says GML can be converted into KML.
HMLR identifies QGIS as free open-source software that can view and convert GML data.
The July 2026 current INSPIRE index explicitly lists both London Borough of Barnet and London Borough of Enfield as local-authority downloads.
The Planning Data API provides access to more than 100 planning and housing datasets for England through one interface.
A Planning Data coordinate query constructs a point from supplied latitude and longitude.
Coordinate search returns entities whose geometry intersects the constructed point.
A coordinate query can include multiple dataset parameters and returns matches from any selected dataset.
The Planning Data q parameter can search by postcode.
The Planning Data q parameter can search by UPRN.
Planning Data recommends UPRN search as more precise than a coordinate for registered properties.
Entity results can include a name field.
Entity results can include a dataset field.
Entity results can include a start-date field.
Entity results can include WKT geometry.
Entity results can include a WKT point.
Planning Data warns that no returned entities does not prove that no planning constraints exist.
Planning Data states that data coverage varies by area.
The documentation's all-local-planning-authority example returns 337 LPAs with limit 500.
The geometry_entity parameter can filter using the geometry of another Planning Data entity.
The geometry_relation value within can be used to find entities contained by another entity's geometry.
Planning Data says its planning-application data specification is currently in development.
Local planning authorities are not currently required to share application data to the developing planning-application specification.
Planning application searches support start_date_year.
Planning application searches support start_date_month.
Planning application searches support start_date_day.
Planning Data documents start_date_match=since for recent-application filtering.
Raw spatial searches accept WKT geometry such as a polygon.
Planning Data says WKT query coordinates should be in WGS84 EPSG:4326.
The geometry_relation parameter supports intersects.
Planning Data uses offset for paging through large entity result sets.
Planning Data recommends incrementing offset by the limit value for successive pages.
Planning Data responses can provide a pre-built next pagination URL.
Planning Data responses can provide a pre-built previous pagination URL.
Planning Data responses can provide a pre-built first pagination URL.
Planning Data responses can provide a pre-built last pagination URL.
The documented portfolio-screening API has no batch endpoint.
Planning Data documents one API request per property for API-based portfolio screening.
Planning Data recommends using field filters to reduce portfolio response payloads.
Planning Data recommends polite rate limiting between per-property requests.
For hundreds of properties or more, Planning Data recommends bulk dataset downloads.
For large portfolios, Planning Data recommends local spatial intersections over downloaded datasets.
Planning Data describes bulk downloads as a stable snapshot and supports CSV, JSON, GeoJSON where applicable and Parquet.
Planning Data states that its API is still beta and may change for production-ready systems.
The Environment Agency LIDAR Composite DTM 1m is a raster elevation model.
The DTM 1m covers approximately 99 percent of England.
The DTM 1m has 1 metre spatial resolution.
The DTM 1m is produced from the last or only laser pulse returned to the sensor.
DTM processing removes surface objects from the DSM to model the terrain surface.
Environment Agency DTM production uses bespoke algorithms to remove surface objects.
Environment Agency DTM production also uses manual editing.
The current DTM 1m composite was produced by the Environment Agency in 2022.
The DTM 1m combines Time Stamped archive surveys with National LIDAR Programme surveys.
Where repeat surveys exist, the newest and best-resolution source is selected for the composite.
Where source data is resampled before merging, the DTM composite uses bilinear interpolation.
The 2022 DTM 1m composite contains surveys beginning 6 June 2000.
The 2022 DTM 1m composite contains surveys through 2 April 2022.
Environment Agency metadata index catalogues identify which survey supplied a location in the composite.
The DTM 1m record provides GeoTIFF raster download capability.
The DTM 1m is distributed using OS National Grid aligned tiling.
DTM elevations are represented in metres.
Environment Agency LIDAR height data is referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn.
Environment Agency LIDAR uses the OSTN15 transformation method in the published composite product chain.
The Environment Agency states LIDAR vertical accuracy of plus or minus 15 centimetres RMSE.
The DTM 1m is available under the Open Government Licence.
The DTM 1m dataset record identifies an annual update frequency.
The DTM 1m coordinate reference system is EPSG:27700.
The DTM 1m metadata identifier is 13787b9a-26a4-4775-8523-806d13af58fc.
The DTM 1m record exposes WMS.
The DTM 1m record exposes WCS.
The DTM 1m record exposes WMTS.
The DTM 1m record exposes an OGC API Features service.
The DTM 1m metadata creation date is 8 February 2023.
The DTM 1m metadata revision date is 15 December 2023.
The DTM 1m geographic extent published by the current record spans approximately latitude 49.943 to 55.816 and longitude -6.236 to 2.072.
The Environment Agency DSM 1m includes object heights such as vehicles, buildings and vegetation as well as terrain.
The DSM 1m covers approximately 99 percent of England at 1 metre resolution.
The DSM 1m is downloadable as GeoTIFF rasters in 5km tiles aligned to the OS National Grid.
The first-return DSM 1m composite record covers source surveys from 11 November 2016.
The first-return DSM 1m composite record covers source surveys through 5 May 2022.
The DTM 2m official record states the same plus or minus 15 centimetres RMSE LIDAR vertical accuracy.
The DTM 2m official record uses EPSG:27700.
The retired 25cm composite DTM record states that the 25cm composite was replaced by a 1m resolution product while time-stamped archive data remains available.
Defra's Data Services Platform announced removal of Esri Image Services in favour of open-standard WCS/WMS services and a move to stable LIDAR feed names without the release-year suffix.
